title: Sai Pallavi and Vijay Sethupathi Have Never Shared a Frame. Mani Ratnam Just Fixed That.
excerpt: Netflix paid ₹20 crore for the streaming rights before a single scene was filmed. AR Rahman has already finished two songs. And the most exciting new pairing in Indian cinema is about to step onto a Mani Ratnam set.
body:
There is a very short list of directors in Indian cinema who can sell a film on reputation alone — before a script leaks, before a poster drops, before a single frame is captured on camera. **Mani Ratnam** is at the top of that list. And he just proved it again.

Netflix has reportedly acquired the digital streaming rights to Ratnam's next directorial — tentatively titled **Production No. 23** — for **₹20 crore**, making it one of the biggest pre-production OTT deals for a content-driven Tamil film this year. The remarkable part? Principal photography hasn't even begun yet. The cameras are expected to roll on **July 5** in Pondicherry and Chennai, with additional segments planned in Europe.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=nZj0_LzlVFE</youtube>


But the ₹20-crore cheque isn't even the most exciting thing about this project. That distinction belongs to the cast.

## The Pairing Nobody Knew They Needed

**Vijay Sethupathi** and **Sai Pallavi** — two of the most magnetic, unpredictable performers working in Indian cinema today — have never appeared on screen together. Not once. In a film industry that recycles its biggest pairings until the chemistry turns to muscle memory, this is a genuinely fresh combination. And Mani Ratnam, the man who turned *Alaipayuthey* into a generational love story, is the one bringing them together.

The film is described as a **mature romantic drama**, with industry insiders already drawing comparisons to *Alaipayuthey* — Ratnam's 2000 masterpiece about the unglamorous reality of young marriage. If Production No. 23 carries even a fraction of that film's emotional precision, we're in for something special.


![Mani Ratnam — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b9/Mani_Ratnam_and_Suhasini_At_The_Vaanam_Kottatum_Audio_Launch2_%28cropped%29.jpg)



> **"The film is already in the green before anyone has called "action."

Is ₹20 crore modest by Mani Ratnam standards?"**



> "The director openly expressed his immense admiration for her acting skills during a promotional event last year."

Sai Pallavi, who can make you cry with a glance and break your heart with a smile, is entering Ratnam's cinematic universe for the very first time. She's currently also filming **Dhanush's D55** and is set to play **Sita** opposite **Ranbir Kapoor** in the two-part epic *Ramayana*. The woman is everywhere — and she should be.

Sethupathi, meanwhile, reunites with Ratnam after their 2018 collaboration on **Chekka Chivantha Vanam**. Between *Maharaja*, *Jailer*, and his relentless slate (he has *Pocket Novel*, *Train*, *Arasan*, *Jailer 2*, and *Slum Dog: 33 Temple Road* in various stages), he remains the hardest-working star in South Indian cinema. But a Mani Ratnam romance asks for something different — vulnerability, restraint, tenderness. If the trailer for this film shows Sethupathi looking at Pallavi the way Ratnam's heroes look at his heroines, the internet will not recover.

## The Business of Confidence

The financial architecture of this film tells its own story. Before a single shot has been composed, Production No. 23 has reportedly locked in a total pre-release business of approximately **₹43 crore**: ₹20 crore for Netflix digital rights, ₹15 crore for audio rights, and ₹8 crore for overseas theatrical distribution (secured by **Home Screen Entertainment**). The film is already in the green before anyone has called "action."

Is ₹20 crore modest by Mani Ratnam standards? Sure — the *Ponniyin Selvan* duology and *Thug Life* commanded higher valuations. But those were spectacles with massive ensemble casts. This is a leaner, character-driven love story with a compact **40-day shooting schedule**. Different scale, different bet — and Netflix clearly likes the odds.

For diaspora audiences, the Netflix deal is the headline that matters most. It means Production No. 23 will be available to stream globally on the platform after its theatrical run, no hunting for regional OTT apps or dodgy stream links. **A new Mani Ratnam film, in your living room in New York or Toronto or London, on the platform you already pay for.**


![Chennai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/32/Chennai_Central.jpg)


## And Then There's Rahman

As if the cast and director weren't enough, **AR Rahman** is firmly on board as composer — extending what is arguably the greatest director-composer partnership in Indian cinema history. From *Roja* to *Bombay* to *Dil Se* to *Ponniyin Selvan*, the Ratnam-Rahman combination has produced some of the most iconic soundtracks ever recorded.

Reports suggest Rahman has already completed **two songs** for the film. The composition work is progressing rapidly, which tracks with the tight 40-day shooting schedule. Early industry whispers had floated the possibility of a different composer stepping in, but those rumours have been firmly put to rest. The Mozart of Madras isn't going anywhere.

The production is backed by **Madras Talkies**, **Lyca Productions**, and **India Talkies** — a formidable combination of Ratnam's own banner, a major South Indian production powerhouse, and a newer player in the space.

## What to Expect

Details about the plot remain closely guarded, though the "mature romantic drama" label and the *Alaipayuthey* comparisons suggest something intimate and emotionally demanding rather than sweeping and epic. Some sources hint at a cop-romance backdrop, but the primary focus is expected to be the intricate dynamics of a modern-day relationship.

With cinematographer **Ravi Varman** expected to lens the project, the visual palette alone will be worth the price of admission. Ratnam's eye for beauty — in faces, in landscapes, in the small gestures between two people falling in love — remains unmatched.

No release date has been announced, but with a 40-day shoot beginning in early July, a late 2026 or early 2027 theatrical release seems plausible. Whenever it arrives, it will arrive on Netflix for global audiences shortly after.

Some films announce themselves with a teaser. This one announced itself with a ₹43-crore business deal and the two best actors in South Indian cinema walking onto the same set for the first time. That's a trailer in itself.
